newsitem.title: ITALY: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Friday, November 8.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Friday, November 8.

text.p: Following are some of the top headlines in leading Italian newspapers.

* Majority parties and opposition could not find an agreement in the Lower House examination of the 1997 budget. The centre-right bloc is fiercely opposed to those articles where the government has asked for proxy powers, which would allow it to dictate policy on several sensitive budget areas without needing parliamentary approval (all).

* Opposition leader Silvio Berlusconi speaks of "tax dictatorship" and says even talks over constitutional reforms are at risk ahead of a street demonstration called for tomorrow by the Freedom Alliance against the budget (all).
* Magistrates in Brescia and La Spezia denied rumours of former magistrate and Public Works minister Antonio Di Pietro being under preliminary investigation in a corruption probe (all).
* Police arrested 22 people in raids across Italy on suspicion of supplying arms, false documents and other support to Algeria's radical Armed Islamic Group (GIA).

* The government is expected to meet again today with hard-left Communist Refoundation party over the sell-off of telecoms state holding Stet. It appears increasingly likely that the sale will not take place before next October, while government is preparing a decree to launch the privatisation of motorways construction and management company Autostrade, which is also owned by state holding company IRI.
* Giorgio Fossa, chairman of the Italian employers association Confindustria says the right central parity for the lira to re-enter the ERM would be 1,050 lire per mark (all).
* Italian investment funds had a net inflow of 7.953 trillion lire in October from 3.408 trillion lire in September (all).
* Italy had a 1.493 trillion lire trade surplus with non-European Union countries in September (all).
Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
